project_type: Electron desktop app 'Intention' (package name 'focusflow' v1.2.2). Renderer is PLAIN HTML/CSS/JS with NO bundler/framework. The renderer files already run in a plain browser and no-op cleanly when window.electronAPI is absent.
language: JavaScript (vanilla, ES5/ES6 style, IIFE modules exposed on window), HTML, CSS
build_system: No front-end build. electron-builder only for desktop installers (node build.js). Do NOT run build.js for this task. Static files are served directly.
test_framework: node:test (node --test). 61 unit tests in test/**/*.test.js covering auth-state, gate, desktop-sync logic (pure, no DOM).
build_command: No front-end build step. For verification, serve statically: python -m http.server 8080 (Python 3.14 is installed) from the repo root c:\Users\sonel\Kiro\productivity-tracker.
test_command: npm test  (runs node --test "test/**/*.test.js"; currently 61 passing, 0 failing). Must stay green.
verification_instructions: 1) Run `npm test` and confirm 61 pass. 2) Start a static server from repo root: `python -m http.server 8080`. 3) Open http://localhost:8080/index.html (web app) and http://localhost:8080/web/ (marketing). 4) In browser DevTools: confirm <html> has class 'web-mode', css/web.css loads 200, and there are NO uncaught console errors from missing electronAPI when navigating Timer/Scheduler/Calendar/History/Read. 5) Test responsive at 375px and 1440px widths. 6) Click nav 'Sign in' (#nav-account) and confirm the auth modal opens. 7) If Electron is runnable, `npm start` must still open in the left-quarter narrow column (all web changes must be scoped so Electron is unaffected).
snapshot_or_generated_files: null - no generated/snapshot files are checked in for front-end.
environment_constraints: Windows + PowerShell. Electron may not be launchable in the sandbox; the Electron narrow-column requirement is 'do not regress' and is satisfied by scoping ALL web changes under html.web-mode (CSS) or `if (!window.electronAPI)` (JS) guards. Do NOT touch main.js, preload.js, the .ps1 helpers, ios/, or dist/.
contribution_requirements: No root AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING. README documents: core features work with no account; optional Supabase email-OTP accounts; MIT license; GitHub repo github.com/sonellmalik/Intention, downloads at https://github.com/sonellmalik/Intention/releases/latest. Preserve existing vanilla-JS code style and intent comments. Only additive or guarded browser-safe changes to the renderer.
key_patterns: Browser detection = absence of window.electronAPI (preload.js exposes it in Electron only; every renderer call is already guarded). Mechanism for this task: a tiny inline script in index.html <head> adds class 'web-mode' to document.documentElement when window.electronAPI is undefined (inline + before stylesheets so no flash). All browser-only CSS lives in a NEW css/web.css linked LAST in index.html and scoped under html.web-mode so Electron defaults are untouched and no !important is needed. There are currently NO @media queries anywhere in css/ - the app assumed a fixed narrow column. Auth is fully browser-safe: js/auth/* uses IIFE modules on window (AuthState, SupabaseClient, SupabaseConfig, AuthGate), auth-ui.js wires #nav-account to openModal and exposes window.openAuthModal; gate.js locks [data-requires-auth]. supabase-config.js already has a REAL project URL + public anon key (isConfigured() === true) so the browser modal runs the real email-OTP flow - do NOT change credentials. supabase-client.js sets persistSession:false (main process owns persistence in Electron); leave it - browser sign-in works per-session without cross-reload persistence, which is acceptable. localStorage keys are prefixed focusflow_ (see js/app.js saveData/loadData). Design tokens in css/style.css :root { --bg:#f8f9fa; --surface:#fff; --text:#1a1a2e; --text-muted:#6c757d; --primary:#4361ee; --primary-hover:#3a56d4; --accent:#f72585; --border:#e9ecef; --radius:10px; --shadow; --shadow-lg; --font:'Segoe UI',-apple-system,...; }. The calendar page (#page-calendar in css/calendar.css) is already width:100% full-width. Breakpoints to use: mobile <=600px, tablet 601-1024px, desktop >=1025px; web-mode content max-width ~1200px centered.
